_meta.purpose: Rules that apply across all uses in the catalogue: when a change of use needs a permit, how requirements are adapted for existing buildings, fire occupancy classes, design occupant densities, accessibility, staff facilities, sanitary provision, ventilation/daylight/acoustics and imposed floor loads. Each entry cites its Swedish source. Read regulatory_status first: Swedish building rules changed on 2025-07-01 (Boverket), 2025-12-01 (PBL permit rules) and change again on 2027-01-01 (PBL/PBF alteration rules).
_meta.use_id_note: The applies_to_uses values are provisional generic ids (e.g. office, housing, student_housing, hotel, school, preschool, elderly_care, healthcare, restaurant, retail, assembly, gym, library, storage, nightclub). 'all' means every use. Align them with the ids in uses/*.json once those files exist.

regulatory_status.summary: BBR (BFS 2011:6) and EKS (BFS 2011:10) have been replaced. Since 2025-07-01 nine Boverket regulations apply, one per technical requirement in PBL 8 kap. 4 §. Most of the dimensional figures that sat in the old BBR 'allmänna råd' (general advice) were removed, so many familiar numbers (2.2 x 2.2 m accessible WC, the occupant-density table, 2.40/2.70 m room heights, SS 25267/25268 sound classes) are no longer in Boverket's building rules. Where the old figures still help, they are recorded below as 'guidance' or 'practice' and labelled as repealed.

new_regulations.title: Boverkets föreskrifter om aktsamhet vid bygg-, rivnings- och markåtgärder
Boverkets föreskrifter och allmänna råd om bärförmåga, stadga och beständighet i byggnader m.m. (replaces EKS, BFS 2011:10)
Boverkets föreskrifter och allmänna råd om säkerhet i händelse av brand i byggnader (replaces BBR section 5)
new_regulations.note: Reportedly amended by BFS 2025:10 from 2025-12-01 (not re-checked here).

new_regulations.title: Boverkets föreskrifter om skydd med hänsyn till hygien, hälsa och miljö samt hushållning med vatten och avfall (replaces BBR section 6)
Boverkets föreskrifter om säkerhet vid användning av byggnader (replaces BBR section 8)
Boverkets föreskrifter om skydd mot buller i byggnader (replaces BBR section 7)
Boverkets föreskrifter om bostäders lämplighet för sitt ändamål (replaces BBR 3:2)
Boverkets föreskrifter om byggnaders tillgänglighet och användbarhet för personer med nedsatt rörelse- eller orienteringsförmåga (replaces BBR 3:1)
Boverkets föreskrifter om krav på tomter m.m.
Stayed in BBR after 2025-07-01. A secondary source reports that a new energy regulation, BFS 2026:9, applies from 2026-10-01. This has not been verified against Boverket.

regulatory_status.transition_boverket: BFS 2024:14 transitional provision 3, as reported by JP Infonet and crewless.io and stated in the final clause of each BFS 2024:x regulation. The old BBR/EKS may be used if the application for bygglov or the anmälan reached the municipality before 2026-07-01, or, where neither is needed, if work started before that date. The old rules must then be used as a whole package; parts of the old and new rules cannot be mixed. If bygglov was granted before 2025-07-01, the old rules apply. Today (2026-10-19) a new permit application therefore falls under the BFS 2024:x regulations.
regulatory_status.pbl_reform_2025: Lag (2025:974) took effect on 2025-12-01 and renumbered and rewrote PBL 9 kap. (permits). Change of use now sits in PBL 9 kap. 15 § 1, not the old 9 kap. 2 § 3 a/b. Cases started before 2025-12-01 stay under the old rules.
regulatory_status.pbl_reform_2027: Lag (2026:746) and Förordning (2026:1265) take effect on 2027-01-01 and rewrite how requirements apply to alterations. New PBL 8 kap. 5 a § says that on a change to a building, the requirements apply to the part that changes, and they SHALL be adapted to the extent reasonable given the scope of the change, the building's conditions, resource conservation and the rules on care and protection of character (varsamhet, förvanskning). New 8 kap. 5 b § introduces 'större byggnadsändring' (replacing 'ombyggnad'): significant health and safety deficiencies under 4 § 1-5 must then be removed in the whole building. PBF 3 kap. 21 § and 23 § are repealed from 2027-01-01.

change_of_use.topic: When a change of use needs bygglov
change_of_use.rule_plain_english: Bygglov is required for a change to a building (other than an extension) if the building, or part of it, is taken into use or fitted out for a substantially different purpose than the one it was last used for. The same applies to the purpose it was last permitted for, if that use never started. Office to housing, school, care, hotel, retail or assembly is normally 'väsentligen annat ändamål'. Adding a dwelling also needs bygglov. Since 2025-12-01 this rule is PBL 9 kap. 15 § 1-2; before that it was 9 kap. 2 § första stycket 3 a-b.

values.exception_outside_plan: PBL 9 kap. 16 § 1: no bygglov when, outside a detaljplan area and outside sammanhållen bebyggelse, premises of at most 50.0 m² gross area in total are fitted out
values.detaljplan_can_add: PBL 9 kap. 2 § andra stycket: a detaljplan or områdesbestämmelser can add further bygglov requirements

change_of_use.source: Plan- och bygglag (2010:900) 9 kap. 2, 15, 16 §§ in the wording of Lag (2025:974), consolidated to SFS 2026:1583
change_of_use.conversion_note: Every office-to-X conversion in a detaljplan area needs bygglov, and the new use must also be consistent with the detaljplan (e.g. B, C, D, K, S). If the plan only allows 'K' (kontor), housing usually needs a planändring or a liten avvikelse. Check the plan first: plan compliance is usually the first blocker, not the building rules.

change_of_use.rule_plain_english: Even when no bygglov is needed, an anmälan to the byggnadsnämnd is required for changes that significantly affect the load-bearing structure or the fire protection, and for installing or significantly changing a lift, fireplace, flue, ventilation, or water and drainage system. A conversion almost always involves at least one of these.
change_of_use.source: Plan- och byggförordning (2011:338) 6 kap. 1 § in the wording of Förordning (2025:979)
change_of_use.conversion_note: Even a use change exempt from bygglov still triggers anmälan, startbesked and a kontrollplan because ventilation, fire protection and often structure change.

change_of_use.topic: Which technical requirements apply when an existing building is changed
change_of_use.rule_plain_english: Only the part that changes must meet today's technical requirements. Each new Boverket regulation (BFS 2024:6-12) has a final chapter on alterations. For a change of use, the scope of the alteration is judged by whether the new use places higher demands than the old one: higher loads, more people, more ventilation, stricter fire, accessibility or acoustic demands. Where it does, those properties must be brought up to standard for the changed part. The old BBR 1:2233 general advice gave examples: significantly increased loads, more people needing changed fire protection or more outdoor air, or a previously unheated space being heated.

values.structure: BFS 2024:6 8 kap. 3 § (explicitly includes 'eventuell ökning av lasteffekter')

change_of_use.conversion_note: This is why 'office to housing' is often easier on structure (the load category drops from B 2.5 to A 2.0 kN/m²) but harder on fire (sleeping occupants), daylight, acoustics and sanitary rooms. 'Office to assembly, gym or retail' is the reverse: loads and egress increase.

change_of_use.topic: Anpassning (adaptation) of requirements for existing buildings
change_of_use.rule_plain_english: The changed part must meet the requirements for new buildings, but the level may be adapted, as long as the result is still acceptable, if this is needed for any of these reasons: (1) to meet the varsamhet (care) requirement; (2) to respect the ban on förvanskning (disfigurement) of especially valuable buildings; (3) full compliance is unreasonable given the scope of the change; (4) compliance would only give a negligible improvement; (5) the cost is unreasonably high relative to the benefit; (6) there are technical reasons; (7) it is needed to achieve acceptable health, safety or accessibility properties, or to protect cultural values. The accessibility regulation is stricter: 'uppenbart oskäligt' (obviously unreasonable) and 'betydande tekniska skäl' (significant technical reasons). A deterioration of existing properties is allowed only if the building still meets the new-build requirements, if it is needed for another requirement or for cultural values, or if it is negligible. The fire regulation also requires a documented risk assessment for any adaptation (BFS 2024:7 1 kap. 14 §).

values.fire: BFS 2024:7 9 kap. 1 § (grounds), 9 kap. 3 § (deterioration), 1 kap. 13-14 §§ (survey of deficiencies, risk assessment)
values.statutory_basis_until_2026_12_31: PBL 8 kap. 7 § (anpassning och avsteg with regard to the scope of the change and the building's conditions; accessibility deviations only if 'uppenbart oskäligt'); PBF 3 kap. 23 § (for accessibility: in an ombyggnad only if obviously unreasonable; in another change, as appropriate to the building's conditions)
values.statutory_basis_from_2027_01_01: PBL 8 kap. 5 a § (requirements SHALL be adapted to the extent reasonable given the scope of the change, the building's conditions, resource conservation, varsamhet/förvanskning); 8 kap. 5 b § (större byggnadsändring: remove significant health and safety deficiencies in the whole building)
values.deferred_compliance: PBF 3 kap. 21 § lets the nämnd defer requirements on other parts of the building in a staged ombyggnad. Repealed 2027-01-01.

change_of_use.conversion_note: This is the main lever in adaptive reuse. The applicant has to argue it: state, for each requirement not met in full, which ground applies and what makes the result acceptable. Fire and accessibility adaptation have hard limits (see fire_change_of_use_floor and access_change_lift). The prompt's 'PBF 3 kap 23-24 §§' is only partly right: 23 § is the accessibility adaptation rule (repealed 2027-01-01); 24 § is Boverket dispensation for experimental building, not general adaptation.

change_of_use.topic: Varsamhet (care) and förbud mot förvanskning (ban on disfigurement)
change_of_use.rule_plain_english: All changes must be carried out with care for the building's character and its technical, historical, cultural-historical, environmental and artistic values (PBL 8 kap. 17 §). Especially valuable buildings must not be disfigured (PBL 8 kap. 13 §). Each BFS 2024:x regulation repeats the same assessment criteria. For varsamhet: proportions, form and volume, materials and workmanship, colour, and level of detail, plus whether the qualities that matter for residents and users are kept. Buildings from before the 1920s building expansion that keep their main character are to be considered especially valuable unless something speaks against it.

values.varsamhet_criteria: BFS 2024:7 9 kap. 5 § (identical in the other BFS 2024:x regulations)

change_of_use.conversion_note: Varsamhet can justify adapting requirements (ground 1), but it also limits facade changes, for example new windows for daylight or new balconies when converting offices to housing. Check the detaljplan for q- or k-markings.

change_of_use.topic: Which rule set applies to a project
change_of_use.rule_plain_english: For applications or anmälan received on or after 2026-07-01, the new BFS 2024:x regulations apply. For earlier applications the builder could choose the old BBR/EKS as a complete package. PBL permit rules: cases started on or after 2025-12-01 follow the rewritten 9 kap. From 2027-01-01 the new alteration rules in PBL 8 kap. 5-5 d §§ apply. A project's rule set is fixed by its application date, so record that date per pilot.
change_of_use.source: BFS 2024:7 final clause 1-2 (in force 2025-07-01, refers to BFS 2024:14 transitional point 3); Lag (2025:974) transitional provisions 1-2; Lag (2026:746)
change_of_use.conversion_note: The exact BFS 2024:14 transitional wording was taken from secondary sources (JP Infonet, crewless.io) and has not been re-read in BFS 2024:14 itself.

fire_occupancy_classes.topic: Verksamhetsklasser (occupancy classes) under BFS 2024:7, and what changed from BBR
fire_occupancy_classes.rule_plain_english: Spaces are classed by four questions: do occupants know the building, can they get to safety on their own, are they awake, and how many are there. BFS 2024:7 2 kap. 9-20 §§ defines Vk 0, 1, 2A, 2B, 2C, 3A, 3B, 3C, 4, 5A, 5B and 5C. Compared with old BBR 5:21: Vk 0 is new (very difficult evacuation, which must be designed by analysis). Old 5D (people held locked in) is now part of Vk 0, point 3. 3C is new (behovsprövat trygghetsboende, sprinkler required). Old Vk 6 (elevated fire-start risk) does not appear as a class in BFS 2024:7. The prescriptive rules (preciserade krav) may only be used for Vk 1-5 in byggnadsklass 1-3.

values.prescriptive_route_allowed_for: Vk 1-5 and byggnadsklass 1-3 (e.g. BFS 2024:7 7 kap. and 8 kap. 5 § andra stycket)

fire_occupancy_classes.source: BFS 2024:7 2 kap. 9-20 §§; BBR (BFS 2011:6, consolidated to BFS 2024:5) 5:21-5:216
fire_occupancy_classes.conversion_note: A conversion that creates Vk 0 (e.g. more than 1,200 visitors, more than 600 with alcohol, more than 150 people who cannot self-evacuate) needs a fully analytical fire design.

fire_occupancy_classes.topic: Vk 0: spaces where evacuation can be very difficult
fire_occupancy_classes.rule_plain_english: Covers (1) more than 1,200 people without good knowledge of the premises; (2) more than 600 such people where alcohol is served beyond a limited extent; (3) spaces where people are held locked in; (4) more than 150 people with limited or no ability to self-evacuate; (5) health care for people who cannot self-evacuate where the activity has more than one functional unit, or evacuation cannot start without delay.
fire_occupancy_classes.conversion_note: Outside the prescriptive route. Large hospital wards and detention also fall here.

fire_occupancy_classes.topic: Vk 1: occupants who know the building, can self-evacuate and are awake
fire_occupancy_classes.rule_plain_english: Industry, offices, residents' storage rooms (lägenhetsförråd) and similar.
fire_occupancy_classes.conversion_note: This is the starting class of most office buildings. Almost every conversion moves to a stricter class: shorter travel distances, alarms, more compartments.

fire_occupancy_classes.topic: Vk 2A, 2B and 2C: public premises with awake occupants unfamiliar with the building
fire_occupancy_classes.rule_plain_english: 2A covers activities with at most 150 people; 2B more than 150; 2C more than 150 with alcohol served beyond a limited extent. Examples in 2A/2B: spaces for pupils in schools, shops, health-centre receptions, assembly rooms, restaurant dining areas, public parts of travel terminals and sports halls. 2C covers larger pubs and nightclubs. Consequences: 2B/2C need an automatic fire alarm (7 kap. 46 §) and an evacuation alarm (acoustic up to 600 people in 2B, spoken message above 600 in 2B and always in 2C; 7 kap. 43-44 §§). 2A-2C need exit signs (7 kap. 39 §). Emergency lighting is required in 2B/2C (7 kap. 40 §), as is a posted sign with the occupant number (always in 2B/2C, in 2A unless unnecessary; 7 kap. 41 §).

values.exit_hardware_2B_2C: emergency exit device up to 1,000 people; panic bar above 1,000 (7 kap. 34 §)

fire_occupancy_classes.conversion_note: An office floor (Vk 1, up to 45 m travel) converted to a school, gym or restaurant must reach a 30 m travel distance (15 m in 2C). Deep office plans with central cores often fail this without new stairs. Sprinkler for occupant protection lets distances grow by one third (doubled in 2C) under 7 kap. 21 §.

fire_occupancy_classes.topic: Vk 3A, 3B and 3C: dwellings (occupants know the building but may be asleep)
fire_occupancy_classes.rule_plain_english: 3A: dwellings in blocks of flats and houses, family day care. 3B: dwellings with boendeenheter (units sharing some dwelling functions) and their shared rooms, e.g. co-living or student corridors. 3C: needs-tested trygghetsboenden and other housing for people who may need support or care part of the day; these residents may have difficulty self-evacuating. 3A needs smoke alarms; 3B needs an automatic fire alarm and an evacuation alarm; 3C needs smoke alarms and the whole building must be sprinklered (automatic water sprinkler for occupant protection or a residential sprinkler system; 7 kap. 47-48 §§). Each dwelling (3A/3C) normally needs two independent exits (7 kap. 9 §); single-stair solutions are allowed under 7 kap. 11 § (Tr1 up to 20 storeys, Tr2 up to 16 storeys, at most 50 persons) or via rescue-service window evacuation (7 kap. 13-15 §§).
fire_occupancy_classes.conversion_note: On change of use to 3A/3B/3C there are no adaptation exceptions for compartmentation (10 kap. 3 §) or for compartmentation of escape routes (10 kap. 2 §), and none for the number of exits (10 kap. 4 §). 3C sprinkler cannot be adapted away either (10 kap. 7 §). Office corridors must be rebuilt as fire-separated escape routes, and every flat becomes its own fire compartment.

fire_occupancy_classes.topic: Vk 4: hotels and temporary lodging (occupants unfamiliar with the building, asleep)
fire_occupancy_classes.rule_plain_english: Guest rooms, dormitories and similar in hotels, hostels, B&Bs and other temporary lodging. Buildings with at least 9 guests or at least 5 guest rooms need an automatic fire alarm and an evacuation alarm (7 kap. 43, 46 §§); smaller ones need smoke alarms (7 kap. 47 §). Each guest room or dormitory needs two exits (7 kap. 9 §), and an evacuation plan must be posted in each room (7 kap. 42 §).
fire_occupancy_classes.conversion_note: Office to hotel: every room becomes its own compartment with no adaptation allowed on change of use (10 kap. 3 §). The 30 m travel distance is stricter than the office's 45 m.

fire_occupancy_classes.topic: Vk 5A, 5B and 5C: people with limited or no ability to self-evacuate
fire_occupancy_classes.rule_plain_english: 5A: preschools, day-activity premises and similar. 5B: dwellings and shared rooms in needs-tested special housing (e.g. SÄBO, LSS group homes). 5C: health care with one functional unit only, where moving patients can start without delay; larger or slower-to-evacuate care is Vk 0. Fire alarm is required in 5A, 5B and 5C (7 kap. 46 §) and an acoustic evacuation alarm in 5A and 5B (7 kap. 43 §). Sprinkler: required in fire compartments with 5B (occupant-protection sprinkler or residential sprinkler system), and in 5C as occupant-protection sprinkler with enhanced reliability (7 kap. 48 §). Every fire compartment in 5A/5B/5C must allow a return route after passage through an exit door (7 kap. 36 §).
fire_occupancy_classes.conversion_note: On change of use, sprinkler in 5B and 5C cannot be adapted away (10 kap. 7 §), and compartmentation in 5A/5B/5C cannot be relaxed (10 kap. 3 §). Budget for sprinkler from day one.

fire_occupancy_classes.rule_plain_english: Class 0: more than 20 storeys above ground or more than 2 storeys below ground (analytical design only). Class 1: 3-20 storeys, except 3-storey one- or two-family houses and ancillary buildings. Class 2: 2 storeys with building footprint over 200 m², or 3-storey one- or two-family houses. Class 3: 1 storey, or 2 storeys with footprint up to 200 m². A top storey where nobody stays permanently is not counted, nor a mezzanine of at most 50% of the floor below and at most 100 m².
fire_occupancy_classes.conversion_note: A change of use does not normally change the building class, but it does change the class-dependent requirements: structural fire resistance (3 kap.) differs for Vk 3A-5C versus Vk 1-2C.

fire_occupancy_classes.topic: Where fire requirements may NOT be relaxed on change of use
fire_occupancy_classes.rule_plain_english: When a space gets a new use, adaptation of the fire safety level is limited. The limits do not apply where compliance would be obviously unreasonable or only a negligible improvement (10 kap. 1 §). No deviation is allowed for: compartmentation of escape routes serving new 3A, 3B, 3C or 5B (2 §); compartmentation where the new use is 3A, 3B, 3C, 4, 5A, 5B or 5C (3 §); number of exits for new 2B, 2C, 3A, 3B, 3C or 5B (4 §); fire and evacuation alarms for any change of use (5 §); exit signs for any change of use (6 §); sprinkler for new 3C, 5B or 5C (7 §); smoke ventilation of stairwells when it is the only access route to the changed space, or serves new 3A, 3B or 3C (8 §); access to riser pipes (stigarledning) for any change of use (9 §).
fire_occupancy_classes.source: BFS 2024:7 10 kap. 1-9 §§ (section 1 reportedly amended by BFS 2025:10)
fire_occupancy_classes.conversion_note: This list is the core of a fire 'fit test' for conversion: if the target use is in the list, treat the item as a hard requirement, not a negotiable adaptation.

fire_occupancy_classes.topic: Exit counts, widths and stair/riser triggers (prescriptive route)
fire_occupancy_classes.rule_plain_english: Number of independent exits per activity: 2 up to 600 persons, 3 for 601-1,000, 4 above 1,000; at least 5 m apart. Clear width of exit doors: 0.80 m for up to 150 persons, 1.15 m above 150, and in total at least 1.00 m per 150 persons. Escape route passages: 0.90 m clear for up to 150 persons, 1.20 m above. Distances are reduced by four times any level difference (7 kap. 22 §). A riser pipe is needed when the most remote floor is more than 24 m above the access point (pressurised above 40 m); a firefighting lift is needed above 30 m (8 kap. 10, 13 §§). The maximum distance from the access route to the most remote point is 50 m, or 80 m with sprinkler (8 kap. 9 §).
fire_occupancy_classes.conversion_note: Total door width (1.0 m per 150 persons) and the 600-person threshold for a third exit usually cap the capacity of an assembly or retail conversion on an office floor.

fire_occupancy_classes.topic: Default variable fire load per use
fire_occupancy_classes.rule_plain_english: The design variable fire load is the 80th percentile for the use, but these fixed values may be used instead: 1,600 MJ/m² for archives, libraries, storage; 1,200 MJ/m² for malls and shopping centres; 600 MJ/m² for cinemas, dwellings, preschools, hotels, offices, food shops, residents' storage rooms, car garages, restaurants, schools, theatre and care premises; 50 MJ/m² for stables, concrete-products industry, breweries and similar.
fire_occupancy_classes.conversion_note: Office to library, archive or storage raises the fire load from 600 to 1,600 MJ/m², which matters for structural fire resistance and compartment walls. Office to housing or school keeps it the same.

occupancy_density.topic: Design number of persons: binding defaults in BFS 2024:7
occupancy_density.rule_plain_english: The design number of persons is the maximum number expected in the space given its use and size. If that is not known, use 0.5 persons/m² for retail premises, 3 persons/m² for pubs and bars, and 2.5 persons/m² for assembly premises. These are the only densities left in the binding text.
occupancy_density.conversion_note: Base area is not specified in the binding text (old BBR used net area). An assembly room at 2.5 persons/m² passes 150 persons, and so moves into Vk 2B, at about 60 m².

occupancy_density.topic: Old BBR table 5:333 design densities (repealed general advice, still useful as a reference)
occupancy_density.rule_plain_english: Old BBR general advice gave design densities in persons per m² of net area. It is repealed for new applications from 2026-07-01 but is still widely used as a starting point in fire strategies. Restaurants used the number of seats or 1.0/m²; fixed-seat assembly used the number of seats. For libraries, conference rooms and restaurants, the net area could exclude loose furniture.
occupancy_density.source: BBR (BFS 2011:6) avsnitt 5:333, tabell 5:333 (allmänt råd, BFS 2011:26); consolidated version to BFS 2024:5, p. 52-53
occupancy_density.conversion_note: Office at 0.1/m² versus classroom at 0.5/m² and restaurant at about 1.0/m²: converting an office floor raises occupant load 5-10 times. That drives exit width, toilets and ventilation. Strength is 'guidance' only for projects under the old BBR; for new applications treat these values as practice.

occupancy_density.rule_plain_english: Neither BFS 2024:7 nor the old BBR table gives a density for gyms, healthcare, preschools, hotels or housing. For these the design number comes from the operator programme: places, beds, rooms. Boverket's analytical design guidance (BBRAD, BFS 2011:27) may contain further values but was not checked here.
occupancy_density.source: BFS 2024:7 2 kap. 4 § (method: the expected maximum number of persons)
occupancy_density.conversion_note: Take occupancy from the use file (occupancy.unit) rather than from area for these uses.

accessibility.topic: Dimensioning wheelchair: plan, turning circle and clear passage
accessibility.rule_plain_english: Where buildings, fixed furniture or equipment must be accessible, design for a wheelchair of 0.70 x 1.30 m, a 1.50 m turning circle and at least 0.80 m clear passage. Inside individual dwellings the figures are smaller: 0.70 x 1.20 m, 1.30 m turning circle and 0.76 m clear passage. The same 1.50 m and 0.80 m figures appear in the fire regulation for wheelchair refuges (BFS 2024:7 2 kap. 32 §) and in the AFS 2023:12 general advice for accessible workplaces.
accessibility.conversion_note: These are binding dimensioning figures (old BBR 3:12 had the same values). Office doors (often 0.8-0.9 m leafs) can fall short of 0.80 m clear passage once frame and leaf thickness are subtracted. Check every door on the accessible route.

accessibility.topic: Level changes, ramps and lifts in new buildings
accessibility.rule_plain_english: Circulation spaces with level changes need a ramp or lift as well as stairs; a lift is required for level changes over 1 m. A ramp may slope at most 1:12, with landings long enough for a wheelchair pushed by a helper. An accessibility lift must fit a wheelchair user plus a helper, with a clear car short side of at least 1,100 mm. Buildings over ten storeys must give access to more than one passenger lift. In dwelling blocks over four storeys a stretcher must fit in a lift (3 kap. 5 §). Under PBF 3 kap. 4 §, dwellings in buildings with fewer than three storeys need not be reached by lift, but a lift must be installable without difficulty.
accessibility.conversion_note: These are new-build rules; for the changed part they apply subject to BFS 2024:12 4 kap. 1 § (adaptation only if obviously unreasonable or for significant technical reasons). Raised office entrance floors and split levels are common blockers.

accessibility.topic: Lift requirement when altering multi-dwelling buildings
accessibility.rule_plain_english: When a multi-dwelling building with more than two storeys is altered, an accessible lift must be installed if there is none and the alteration includes major work in the stairwell, a re-planned layout or extensive work on the structure. Exceptions apply for förvanskning, negligible improvement, significant technical reasons, health and safety or cultural values, or if a lift is unsuitable for residential quality. From 2027-01-01 a new PBF 3 kap. 4 b § says that a building with fewer than four storeys after a change need not get a lift to make dwellings accessible, though an existing lift may not be taken out of use.
accessibility.source: BFS 2024:12 4 kap. 5 §; PBF 3 kap. 4 b § (Förordning 2026:1265, in force 2027-01-01)
accessibility.conversion_note: Office buildings usually already have lifts, but check car size (1,100 mm short side) and whether every new dwelling level is served. How BFS 2024:12 4 kap. 5 § (more than 2 storeys) interacts with the new PBF 4 b § (fewer than 4 storeys) from 2027 is unclear; see open_questions.

accessibility.topic: Accessible WC in public premises (publik lokal)
accessibility.rule_plain_english: If a public premises has toilets for the public, at least one must be accessible, with room to turn a wheelchair and for sideways transfer between toilet and wheelchair on both sides. Its fixed furniture and equipment must be usable by people with limited mobility or orientation ability. BFS 2024:12 gives no room size. The old BBR 3:1453 general advice said at least 2.2 x 2.2 m and, in premises with public WCs on several floors, one accessible WC per such floor.
accessibility.source: BFS 2024:12 2 kap. 7 §, 3 kap. 7 §; old BBR (BFS 2011:6) 3:1453 allmänt råd (repealed)
accessibility.conversion_note: The 2.2 x 2.2 m figure lives on in AFS 2023:12 3 kap. 58 § (general advice) for workplaces. It is a safe planning value: about 4.8 m² per accessible WC. Note: the prompt's 'BBR 3:146' is actually accessibility in single-level dwellings; the public WC rule was 3:1453.

accessibility.rule_plain_english: In public premises where the sound environment is essential for people with limited orientation ability to receive important information, it must be designed for good audibility, speech intelligibility and orientation. Assembly halls and receptions must have a hearing-loop or similar sound transfer system. Not all audience places in an assembly hall need to be wheelchair-accessible. Main entrances must be accessible and clearly perceivable.
accessibility.conversion_note: Hearing loops in receptions are cheap to add but often forgotten in office-to-clinic or office-to-library conversions.

accessibility.rule_plain_english: At least one hygiene room per dwelling must be accessible, with space for fixed fittings. Kitchens must have space for fittings that can be made accessible. In at least one sleeping room it must be possible to arrange free space for assistance along both long sides and at the foot of a bed; in housing with boendeenheter this applies in every unit, but not in student housing. In multi-level dwellings at least the entrance level must be accessible. A stretcher must be able to reach every dwelling or boendeenhet. PBL 8 kap. 6 § lets up to 80% of student dwellings in a building be exempt from accessibility, though they must still be visitable.
accessibility.conversion_note: The 80% student-housing exemption is a major enabler for compact office-to-student-housing conversions.

accessibility.rule_plain_english: The PBL accessibility requirements do not apply to a work premises (arbetslokal) where they are unjustified given the type of activity. Separately, AFS 2023:12 requires existing workplaces to be accessible to employees who need it. In new builds and ombyggnad, workplaces must be designed for a small outdoor electric wheelchair, with at least one accessible WC per floor.
accessibility.source: PBL 8 kap. 6 § första stycket 1; AFS 2023:12 3 kap. 3-4 §§
accessibility.conversion_note: Staff areas in any converted use (school, care, retail back-of-house) fall under AFS 2023:12 3 kap. 4 §, which requires one accessible WC per floor when a building is newly built or rebuilt.

accessibility.topic: Enkelt avhjälpta hinder (easily remedied obstacles) in existing public premises: HIN
accessibility.rule_plain_english: Retroactive rule: in existing public premises and public places, obstacles that are easy to remedy given practical and economic conditions must be removed. Covered obstacles include small level differences, heavy doors and poorly placed controls; missing contrast or warning markings; poor signage; poor sound environment; poor or glaring lighting; missing handrails; poorly designed fixed furniture (e.g. hygiene rooms); and, on public places, accessible parking. The general advice includes: ramps no steeper than 1:12, with 1:20 or flatter preferred; a light-reflectance contrast of at least 0.40 (NCS) on stairs and glazed areas; handrails extending at least 30 cm beyond the stair or ramp; and door-opener push buttons centred about 80 cm above floor and at least 70 cm from corners.
accessibility.source: Boverkets föreskrifter och allmänna råd (2011:13) om avhjälpande av enkelt avhjälpta hinder till och i lokaler dit allmänheten har tillträde och på allmänna platser, HIN 3 (amended by BFS 2013:9), 5-17 §§ (ramp, contrast and handrail values are allmänt råd = guidance); PBL 8 kap. 12 § andra stycket
accessibility.conversion_note: HIN applies to existing public premises even without a building permit, and the first public use after conversion triggers it. HIN is not among the BFS 2024:x regulations; it appears to still apply, and a secondary source mentions new PBL provisions on enkelt avhjälpta hinder from 2027-01-01 (Lag 2026:746). Not verified; see open_questions.

accessibility.topic: Accessibility of public places (allmänna platser): ALM
accessibility.rule_plain_english: Boverket's regulations on accessibility and usability of public places and areas for buildings other than buildings (ALM 2, BFS 2011:5) apply to new or changed public places. They matter for conversion only where the project also changes adjoining public space or site paths.
accessibility.conversion_note: Status after the 2025 reform not verified (it may be affected by BFS 2024:13 'krav på tomter m.m.'). See open_questions.

staff_facilities.rule_plain_english: AFS 2023:12 'Utformning av arbetsplatser' took effect on 2025-01-01 and repealed AFS 2020:1 'Arbetsplatsens utformning', as part of the Work Environment Authority's restructured AFS series. Personalutrymmen (staff facilities) are covered by 3 kap. 37-65 §§. The employer is responsible; the designer is responsible for 3 kap. 4 § (accessible workplaces in new builds and ombyggnad).
staff_facilities.conversion_note: Every use with employees (school, care, hotel, shop, gym) needs staff facilities on top of the user-facing programme. Do not forget them in the area schedule.

staff_facilities.topic: Staff facilities: number, location and size
staff_facilities.rule_plain_english: The number, location, size and furnishing of staff facilities must suit the type and duration of work, the number of employees normally using them at the same time, and their functional ability. They must be easy to reach and may not be used for activities or storage that reduce their usefulness. No m² values are given.
staff_facilities.conversion_note: Size is 'strength: none' at law level; take m² from operator programmes.

staff_facilities.topic: Clothes storage, changing rooms and showers
staff_facilities.rule_plain_english: There must be storage for private clothes, lockable if kept in changing rooms, plus lockable storage for valuables. Changing rooms (or another suitable space, such as a roomy toilet) are required for dirty or sweaty work or where special work clothes must be worn. Changing rooms must normally be separate for men and women if used at the same time, with seats for those who normally sit at the same time. A shower is normally required for sweaty or dirty work and always where there is a risk of infection or strong-smelling or hazardous substances; the shower must be in a washroom next to the changing rooms.
staff_facilities.conversion_note: Care, preschool and kitchen staff wear work clothes, so they need changing rooms with showers. Office conversions rarely have the drainage in place for these; that is a plumbing (services layer) cost.

staff_facilities.topic: Eating space, pause space, rest room and on-call room
staff_facilities.rule_plain_english: Employees must be able to eat in suitable spaces with tables and chairs with backrests, with a fridge, food heating and dishwashing nearby. There must be a place for pauses with enough seats with backrests. A rest space for temporary, undisturbed lying-down rest must exist or be quick to arrange. General advice: a dedicated rest room may be needed when more than 50 people work at the same time in the same area, with a toilet nearby. Staff on on-call duty (jour) need an undisturbed single on-call room, with a toilet and shower nearby.
staff_facilities.source: AFS 2023:12 3 kap. 60-65 §§ (the over-50 threshold is allmänt råd = guidance)
staff_facilities.conversion_note: On-call rooms matter for 24/7 care (SÄBO, LSS, healthcare).

staff_facilities.topic: Room height, daylight and outlook at workplaces
staff_facilities.rule_plain_english: Workplaces must have enough area and free height to limit risk of ill health. General advice: room height at least 2.40 m; in limited parts, at least 2.10 m under horizontal ceilings or 1.90 m under sloping ceilings where standing height is needed; at least 2.70 m in teaching rooms and rooms for larger numbers of people. Workplaces must give satisfactory daylight and outlook during the working day. If that is impossible because neither rebuilding nor moving is reasonable, or because of the type of activity, compensating measures are required. SS-EN 17037:2018 is referenced as an example assessment method.
staff_facilities.source: AFS 2023:12 3 kap. 5 § (heights are allmänt råd); 5 kap. 25 §
staff_facilities.conversion_note: The daylight and outlook duty applies to permanent workplaces in every converted use. Deep office cores turned into staff rooms or back-of-house need a justification. With Boverket's room-height figures removed (old BBR 3:3112-3:3113: 2.70 m in public premises), the AFS 2.70 m advice for teaching rooms is now the main national reference for schools.

staff_facilities.rule_plain_english: No m² per employee is set; only 'sufficient area and free height' (3 kap. 5 §) and normally a free working space of at least 0.8 m where work involves force, twisting, crouching or bending (3 kap. 6 §).
staff_facilities.conversion_note: A size of null with strength 'none' is the honest answer for m² per workplace.

sanitary.rule_plain_english: Every dwelling must have a room for personal hygiene with fixed fittings for hygiene. At least one hygiene room must be accessible (BFS 2024:12 2 kap. 9 §). In housing with boendeenheter (one-person units), a hygiene room may be shared by at most three units; it must be on the same floor as, and adjacent to, those units. This sharing is not allowed in särskilda boendeformer för äldre or special housing for disabled people (2 kap. 10-11 §§). Laundry may be shared and outside the dwelling, sized for the dwellings sharing it.
sanitary.conversion_note: Shared bathrooms (1 per 3 units) are a strong enabler for co-living or student conversion of offices with few drainage risers: fewer bathrooms means fewer new vertical drains.

sanitary.rule_plain_english: There must be enough toilets and washbasins, normally near the workplace, pause spaces, changing and shower rooms. Toilet rooms must be large enough, separate, have a lockable door and no direct connection to an eating space, with a washbasin in or next to the room. General advice: one toilet per started group of 15 employees. Existing workplaces must have toilets accessible to all who need them; general advice: at least 2.2 x 2.2 m, with alarm, contrast markings and suitable fittings. In new builds and ombyggnad, at least one accessible toilet per floor.
sanitary.source: AFS 2023:12 3 kap. 4 § p. 6, 56-58 §§ (1/15 and 2.2 x 2.2 m are allmänt råd = guidance)
sanitary.conversion_note: Staff WC count = ceil(staff_on_site / 15), separate from any public WC count.

sanitary.topic: Toilets for the public in public premises
sanitary.rule_plain_english: Boverket's rules do not say WHEN public toilets are required or HOW MANY. They only say that if public toilets exist, at least one must be accessible. Whether and how many follows from other legislation, e.g. the food-premises rules for restaurants, the Skollagen and AFS for schools, and municipal programmes, or from practice.
sanitary.conversion_note: Public WC counts must come from the use files (operator or municipal programme, or practice), not from national law.

sanitary.topic: Water and drainage installations on alteration
sanitary.rule_plain_english: When a building is altered, the changed part must meet the water and drainage requirements (BFS 2024:8 8 kap. 3-6 §§). These may be adapted only if the improvement would be negligible. Installations taken out of use must be dismantled or plugged as close to the live pipe as possible.
sanitary.conversion_note: Little room for adaptation, so plan new wet rooms around existing drainage risers.

ventilation_daylight_acoustics.rule_plain_english: Ventilation systems in dwellings must be designed for an outdoor-air flow of at least 0.35 l/s per m² floor area, and at least 4.0 l/s per person for rooms. Dwellings must allow increased air exchange, and cooking pollutants must be captured at source. In the new rules the 0.35 figure applies only to dwellings; for other buildings the requirement is functional ('acceptable air quality for the intended use', 3 kap. 1, 4 §§).
ventilation_daylight_acoustics.source: BFS 2024:8 3 kap. 2, 4-6 §§; old BBR 6:251 (0.35 l/s per m² for all buildings)
ventilation_daylight_acoustics.conversion_note: Office systems usually far exceed 0.35 l/s/m², but they are designed for daytime only and without kitchen extraction per unit. Housing needs continuous 24/7 ventilation and cooker hoods: often new risers or per-flat FTX.

ventilation_daylight_acoustics.rule_plain_english: Indoor workplaces must normally be able to receive at least 7 l/s outdoor air per person plus at least 0.35 l/s per m² floor area while work is going on.
ventilation_daylight_acoustics.conversion_note: Pupils and visitors are not employees, but this per-person figure is the usual design basis for schools and premises (via Folkhälsomyndigheten guidance, not checked here). Raising density from office (0.1 p/m²) to classroom (0.5 p/m²) needs roughly 2.5-3x the air flow, often the binding constraint in shafts and plant rooms.

ventilation_daylight_acoustics.rule_plain_english: When use changes, the scope of the alteration is judged by whether the new use demands more air exchange than the old one. Ventilation ducts taken out of use must be dismantled or sealed.
ventilation_daylight_acoustics.conversion_note: Any density increase triggers a ventilation upgrade for the changed part.

ventilation_daylight_acoustics.topic: Daylight in dwellings, including conversion of premises to dwellings
ventilation_daylight_acoustics.rule_plain_english: New dwellings must have daylight corresponding to a daylight factor of at least 1.0% for at least half of the summed assessed area of all rooms where people stay more than temporarily. In shared housing, this applies in each unit and in the shared rooms. Living and eating spaces must have outlook (not required in shared spaces for one-person units). When premises not previously used as dwellings are converted to dwellings, the 1.0% rule applies to the changed part. If one of the general adaptation grounds applies, 0.8% may be accepted, and further adaptation is allowed only if the improvement would be negligible or to avoid disfiguring an especially valuable building. This replaces old BBR 6:322, which had a functional rule plus general advice (10% glass-to-floor ratio, about 1% DF, per SS 91 42 01) per room.
ventilation_daylight_acoustics.conversion_note: This is the binding constraint for office-to-housing: deep floor plates (over about 12-14 m) cannot reach 1.0% (or 0.8%) DF on half the area. It is a dwelling-level, area-weighted rule, so plan depth and window height count. Calculation method: see open_questions.

ventilation_daylight_acoustics.topic: Daylight in premises (lokaler) and room height
ventilation_daylight_acoustics.rule_plain_english: Rooms in premises where people stay more than temporarily must allow enough daylight and outlook to avoid harm to health, unless unreasonable given the room's use. Room height must be enough to avoid harm and suit the use; no figure is given. The old BBR 3:311 required 2.40 m in dwellings and working rooms, and 2.70 m in public premises (2.40 m allowed in rooms for few people, at most 16 persons according to the general advice).
ventilation_daylight_acoustics.conversion_note: Treat old BBR heights as 'practice' for new applications. Office floor-to-ceiling heights (often 2.6-2.7 m under suspended ceilings) are usually adequate.

ventilation_daylight_acoustics.topic: Sound insulation and noise limits in dwellings
ventilation_daylight_acoustics.rule_plain_english: BFS 2024:10 now writes the minimum values directly instead of pointing to sound class C in SS 25267. Airborne sound insulation into dwellings: DnT,w,50 at least 56 dB from commercial premises, shared service rooms and garages; at least 52 dB from other spaces; DnT,w,100 at least 44 dB from stairwells and corridors. Impact sound: L'nT,w,50 at most 52 dB from premises, 56 dB from other spaces, 62 dB from stairwells and corridors. Installation noise in rooms for sleeping or daily living: LAeq 30 dB (25 dB for tonal noise), LAFmax 35 dB. Traffic noise indoors: LAeq 30 dB and night LAFmax 45 dB. Separate tables apply for student housing with boendeenheter (e.g. 48 dB between units) and housing for the elderly.
ventilation_daylight_acoustics.conversion_note: Mixed use (shops, gym or restaurant below flats) needs DnT,w,50 of at least 56 dB and L'nT,w,50 of at most 52 dB. Office hollow-core or lightweight slabs with raised floors often fail impact sound without floating screeds.

ventilation_daylight_acoustics.rule_plain_english: For premises, BFS 2024:10 is functional: spaces must dampen noise as the intended use requires, considering sound insulation, impact sound, installation noise, external noise and reverberation time. The old BBR general advice (7:22) deemed the rules met if the building-related requirements of sound class C in SS 25268 were achieved. That reference has been removed, but SS 25268 class C remains the de facto design level in practice.

values.de_facto_standard: SS 25268 ljudklass C (purchasable SIS standard, values not reproduced)

ventilation_daylight_acoustics.source: BFS 2024:10 2 kap. 9 §; old BBR 7:22 allmänt råd (repealed)
ventilation_daylight_acoustics.conversion_note: SS 25267 and SS 25268 are copyrighted SIS standards; their values are not published here.

structural_loads.topic: Imposed floor loads by use category (replaces EKS / SS-EN 1991-1-1 national choices)
structural_loads.rule_plain_english: Characteristic imposed loads from furniture, goods and people. Each entry gives the uniformly distributed load on floors, stairs and balconies (kN/m²), the concentrated load (kN), and the concentrated load on stairs in brackets. Category A, rooms in dwellings: 2.0 / 2.0 / 3.5 kN/m², 2.0 kN (2.0). Dwelling attics at least 0.6 m high: 1.0 kN/m², 1.5 kN; attics reached only by a hatch of at most 1 m²: 0.5 kN/m², 0.5 kN. B, offices: 2.5 / 3.0 / 3.5, 3.0 (3.0). C1, assembly with movable seats: 2.5 / 3.0 / 2.5, 3.0 (3.0). C2, fixed seats: 2.5 / 3.0 / 2.5, 3.0 (3.0). C3, assembly without obstacles to moving people: 3.0 / 3.0 / 3.0, 3.0 (3.0). C4, assembly with physical activity: 4.0 / 3.0 / 4.0, 4.0 (3.0). C5, possible large crowds: 5.0 / 5.0 / 5.0, 4.5 (4.5). D1, retail: 4.0 / 3.0 / 4.0, 4.0 (3.0). D2, department stores: 5.0 / 3.0 / 5.0, 7.0 (3.0). E1, spaces where goods may accumulate, including circulation: 5.0 / 5.0 / 5.0, 7.0 (3.0). Storage loads are the higher of the actual goods weight and E1. Floors with several uses are designed for the most unfavourable one.

use_to_category_mapping_suggested.hotel_rooms: A (indicative: Eurocode convention puts hotel rooms in A; not stated in BFS 2024:6)

structural_loads.conversion_note: This matters most for office conversions. B (2.5 kN/m²) to A (2.0) frees capacity, which can carry new screeds, wet rooms and partitions. B to C1/C2 (2.5) is load-neutral, but B to C3 (3.0), C4 gym (4.0), D1 retail (4.0), C5 (5.0) or E1 storage, archive or library stacks (5.0) is a 20-100% increase and usually needs structural verification or strengthening. Under BFS 2024:6 8 kap. 3 § this load increase is exactly what makes the change 'require higher properties'. The use-to-category mapping marked 'indicative' is a convention, not stated in BFS 2024:6.

structural_loads.topic: Area and storey reduction of imposed loads
structural_loads.rule_plain_english: For categories A-D, a member carrying more than 20 m² may reduce the distributed imposed load by alpha_A (with a minimum of 0.6 for C and D). A member carrying more than two storeys may reduce it per storey by alpha_n. For dwellings and offices both factors may be combined, but alpha_A x alpha_n may not go below 0.5. The formulas are given in BFS 2024:6 4 kap. 14-15 §§ (text extraction lost the fraction bars; read as alpha_A = 0.5 + 10/A <= 1.0 and alpha_n = 0.7 + 0.6/n <= 1.0, to be checked in the PDF).
structural_loads.conversion_note: The reduction for columns and foundations in tall office buildings may disappear when floors change to C or D categories, because the alpha_A x alpha_n combination is only allowed for dwellings and offices.

structural_loads.topic: Horizontal line loads on barriers and escape-stair loads
structural_loads.rule_plain_english: Horizontal line load on guard rails, barriers and partitions: 0.5 kN/m for A, B and C1; 1.0 kN/m for C2, C3, C4 and D; 3.0 kN/m for C5; 2.0 kN/m for E. Walls, flights and landings in stairwells that are the only escape route: 4 kN/m² on walls and 8 kN/m² on flights and landings in buildings of at most 8 storeys; 6 and 12 kN/m² above 8 storeys.
structural_loads.conversion_note: Office balustrades and atria (0.5 kN/m) converted to assembly, retail or gym need 1.0-3.0 kN/m: check glass balustrades.

structural_loads.rule_plain_english: The changed part must meet BFS 2024:6 chapters 2-7, with the standard adaptation grounds. On change of use, the scope is judged by whether the new use demands more load-bearing capacity, including any increase in load effects. Existing-building experience may be used in design (1 kap.), and structural documentation is not needed on alteration if unnecessary.
structural_loads.conversion_note: Load-category upgrades are not something adaptation can waive lightly: ground 7 (health and safety) works against it.

open_questions: BFS 2025:10 amended BFS 2024:7 from 2025-12-01 (secondary sources). This file used the original BFS 2024:7 text. Re-check the changed paragraphs, especially 10 kap. 1 § and any changed class definitions, against Boverket's consolidated version.
Energy: secondary source claims BFS 2026:9 replaced BBR section 9 from 2026-10-01, with old rules usable for applications before 2027-10-01. Not verified on boverket.se.
Old Vk 6 (elevated fire-start risk) is not a class in BFS 2024:7. Confirm how such spaces are handled now (likely through fire load and protection against fire start in 4 kap.).
BFS 2024:14 transitional point 3 was taken from secondary sources (JP Infonet, crewless.io). Read the primary text to confirm the 2026-07-01 cut-off and the all-or-nothing rule.

PBL/PBF from 2027-01-01 (Lag 2026:746, Förordning 2026:1265): the new 8 kap. 5 a-5 b §§ ('större byggnadsändring', mandatory removal of significant health and safety deficiencies) will change how conversions are assessed. Boverket's alteration chapters in BFS 2024:x may be revised to match. Re-check in January 2027.

From 2027-01-01, PBF 3 kap. 4 b § says no lift is needed for dwellings after a change if the building has fewer than 4 storeys. BFS 2024:12 4 kap. 5 § requires one in multi-dwelling buildings with more than 2 storeys on major alterations. The interaction needs checking.

HIN (BFS 2011:13) and ALM (BFS 2011:5): confirm they remain in force after the 2025 reform and whether BFS 2024:13 or Lag 2026:746 (from 2027-01-01) changes them. The PBL paragraph HIN relies on for public premises (8 kap. 2 § andra stycket) was not re-checked in the post-2025:974 PBL.

BFS 2024:8 4 kap. 1 §: the DF method (calculation standard, reference plane, 'bedömd yta') is in Boverket guidance, not the regulation text. Find the PBL kunskapsbanken guidance on how to verify 1.0% / 0.8% DF over half the area.

BFS 2024:6: the reduction formulas (alpha_A, alpha_n) were read from garbled PDF text. Verify. Also check whether BFS 2024:6 sets a value for movable partitions (the EN 1991-1-1 6.3.1.2(8) equivalent), which matters for office-to-housing.

Did the old EKS values for category A (dwellings) differ from BFS 2024:6's 2.0 kN/m²? Not checked. If EKS used a lower value, buildings designed as housing under EKS may lack margin for today's category A.
The use-to-load-category mapping for school, restaurant, library and hotel is a Eurocode convention, not stated in BFS 2024:6. Confirm with Boverket guidance.

Occupant densities for gym, healthcare, preschool and hotel are not in any binding or general-advice text found. Check BBRAD (BFS 2011:27) and its successor under BFS 2024:7 (analytical design guidance, SIS/TS 24837:2024 is referenced).
Ventilation per person in schools and public premises (as opposed to workplaces): Folkhälsomyndigheten's general advice (FoHMFS 2014:18) was not checked.
AFS 2023:12 may have been amended after 2025-01-01 (the PDF read is the base text). Check the av.se consolidated version.
Public WC counts (retail, restaurant, assembly) have no national rule. Source them from municipal or operator programmes, or the food-premises rules, in the individual use files.
